chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

about the meaning of 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim'; he (AS) responded: The Ba is the brilliance of Allah, the Sin is the splendor of Allah, and the Mim is the magnificence of Allah. And some have narrated: it is the Kingdom of Allah. Allah is the God of everything. Al-Rahman is [Merciful] to all His creation, and Al-Rahim is [Merciful] to the believers specifically.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning of the letters Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a key example of *ta'wil* (esoteric interpretation), attributing the letters of the Basmala to divine attributes rather than mere phonetics, a view supported by the Ismaili scholar Al-Qasim ibn Yahya. The distinction between *Al-Rahman* (universal mercy for all creation) and *Al-Rahim* (specific mercy for the believers) underscores the dual nature of divine grace in Shia theology. This interpretation elevates the Basmala from a ritual opening to a profound declaration of God's ontological perfection.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Yahya, on the authority of his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Sinan that I asked Abut `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) about the meaning of Bismillah al-Rahman alRahim;

hence, he (AS) responded, The Ba * is the brilliance {baha] of Allah. The sin * is the splendor [sama] of Allah. The mim * is the magnificence [majd] of Allah, and some have related that it is the Kingdom [mulk] of Allah. Allah is the God of Everything. AlRahman is the Beneficent to all His creation, an al-Rahim is the One who is Merciful to the Believes specifically.
